div.div: Bob gets his own connection. The same registry entry serves every user, and each one authorizes separately against their own upstream account. That is the point of this mode: one server definition, many individual identities, and nothing shared between them.

switch.text: Bob gets his own connection. The same registry entry serves every user, and each one authorizes separately against their own upstream account. That is the point of this mode: one server definition, many individual identities, and nothing shared between them.

div.div: No client secret is stored in the registry entry, and no operator ever handles a user's upstream credential. Revoking one person means disconnecting that person, not rotating a shared key.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 446px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#333333, #c1c1c1); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
A Service key is tied to nobody. The request arrives with no user identity, so
there is no one for the gateway to send to a consent screen and no per-user
token to look up. The call stops at step 2 above.
The symptom is a 500 reading Unable to verify user access, which reads as a
permissions problem and sends people to check roles and tool provisioning.
The cause is the kind of credential, not its scope.
A key's type is fixed at creation and cannot be converted. Fixing this means
issuing a User key and redeploying whatever held the old one, so settle the
key type before building the registry entry.

text.tspan: A Service key is tied to nobody. The request arrives with no user identity, so
there is no one for the gateway to send to a consent screen and no per-user
token to look up. The call stops at step 2 above.
The symptom is a 500 reading Unable to verify user access, which reads as a
permissions problem and sends people to check roles and tool provisioning.
The cause is the kind of credential, not its scope.
A key's type is fixed at creation and cannot be converted. Fixing this means
issuing a User key and redeploying whatever held the old one, so settle the
key type before building the registry entry.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 446px; margin-left: 751px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#333333, #c1c1c1); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Step 3 normally works because the gateway registers itself with the service
automatically, through dynamic client registration. Some services refuse:
Snowflake, and anything fronted by an enterprise identity provider such as
Okta or Entra.
The error is Incompatible auth server: does not support
dynamic client registration.
The fix is to create an OAuth client with the service yourself and hand the
gateway its client ID and secret through Advanced Settings. That is the only
case where this mode needs an operator to type anything.

text.tspan: Step 3 normally works because the gateway registers itself with the service
automatically, through dynamic client registration. Some services refuse:
Snowflake, and anything fronted by an enterprise identity provider such as
Okta or Entra.
The error is Incompatible auth server: does not support
dynamic client registration.
The fix is to create an OAuth client with the service yourself and hand the
gateway its client ID and secret through Advanced Settings. That is the only
case where this mode needs an operator to type anything.

div.b: Wrapper in the OAuth Metadata box
div.span:
Everything nests one level too deep. The gateway
finds no client_id, falls back to dynamic client
registration without reporting it, and the original
error returns.
The credentials look correct in the console the
whole time, which is what makes this expensive.
